12-reactive.errors.rip.why: the := lowering's satisfies guard — the second publish of the wrong-initializer double, mapped onto the annotation span; asserts the interim while the double-publish row is open (FINDINGS.md)
the ~= lowering's value-level second publish on the derivation expression; asserts the interim while the double-publish row is open (FINDINGS.md)

13-components.errors.rip.why: the ref-cell mismatch (an HTMLInputElement cell on a div) — rip-native: React's ref rejection fires for a different reason (a raw element is not a Ref shape), so the twin cannot honestly judge it; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

the two-way bind mismatch (number state into a string prop) — no TSX line can spell the <=> channel; the container-typed message is the channel's real contract; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

a wrong-typed member write in the `@` spelling — the diagnostic anchors on the sigil (the lowering's `this` maps back through the member's own cover), and no TSX line spells `@`, so the twin cannot transfer the position; the bare spelling one line above is the derived pair

14-schema.errors.rip.why: a wrong-typed field default — rip states the relation as a `satisfies` on the descriptor's own value (TS1360), while zod states it as an argument type (TS2345), so the twin's line carries a CORRECT default and stays quiet rather than deriving a code rip never publishes

25-components.errors.rip.why: the non-nullable ref cell's own initializer — the declaration is deliberately un-nullable so the ref row below can reject, and `:=` takes an initializer, so the same deliberate wrongness reports twice: once here and once at the ref; the TSX twin spells the cell nullable (useRef<T | null>) and carries neither

a non-nullable cell receiving an element ref — the cell's own nullability is what rejects, and React's ref rejection fires for a different reason (a raw element is not a Ref shape), so the twin cannot honestly judge it; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)
a tag-typed cell on a foreign tag — the same rip-native ref surface as the row above, one tag apart; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

a forwarded element ref whose cell types a different tag than the child's own ref — no TSX line can spell the <=> channel, and the container-typed message is the channel's real contract; pinned per the components ruling (RULINGS.md)

an array-typed reactive member whose initializer carries a wrong element — the mismatch rip publishes is between CELLS (the declared `{value: string[]}` against the inferred `{value: (string | number)[]}`), so it anchors on the member rather than on the element the twin flags; the twin's own array is correct and stays quiet

11-types.errors.rip.why: an import type naming a module nothing answers — the specifier lives inside opaque TYPE TEXT, which carries no per-token spans, so the diagnostic covers the annotation where TypeScript's own anchors on the string; the twin's line spells a RESOLVING import type instead, so it witnesses the construct while staying quiet rather than deriving a position rip cannot reach. A specifier that resolves for BOTH judges cannot exist in this lane (10-modules.errors.rip states why)
